title: Ghost DOM generator + exposure modes
goal: state → a perfect semantic tree (h1–h3, p, ul>li, strong, em, br) keyed by block id, updated incrementally, with the D3 exposure modes.
scope: ghost(state) via createElement/textContent; consecutive li grouped into one ul; canonical mark nesting (strong outside em), adjacent equal runs merged
Incremental update by block id + version
Exposure switch: inert (Fluid edit and read) vs .sr-only exposed with aria-hidden projection (for non-semantic projections, tested with a stub)
.sr-only CSS (clip-path inset(50%), 1px box, overflow hidden, white-space nowrap)

rules.rule: Ghost DOM only via DOM APIs, never HTML strings.
Same state → byte-identical ghost markup on all targets.

criteria: For 1000 random states the ghost outerHTML is identical across all 5 targets and equals stored goldens for the fixture states.
Editing one block changes only that block’s ghost node (MutationObserver count).
With the stub projection, the a11y snapshot shows correct heading levels, one list with N items and paragraphs; every text exactly once.
In Fluid mode the ghost is inert: not in the a11y tree; window.find on a unique word finds exactly 1 match on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
axe-core: 0 serious/critical violations in edit and read mode.
acceptance.critic: Criteria-based; the gap is the first unproven criterion.
